question: Does the guard of the one-birth-at-a-time study still build what the complete rounds build under the cap of three as recorded for the ring that returns, with the fillers, and when knots hold instead of releasing; and where it does not, at which birth does it first differ?
inputs: The starts, laws, guards, cutoffs and kinds of order named in the pre-registration; this epic's definitions, the definitions of LOCAL-ROUND-20261123-001 and the shared definitions; the engine of LOCAL-ROUND-20261123-001A, extended; the ring study's engine, unchanged, as the reference.
forbidden_inputs: Any definition changed after a value is seen; any change to the reference engine; any time budget in place of a registered cap.
primary_observable: For every start, law, guard, cutoff and kind of order: whether each order matches, mismatches or underbuilds; the least number of births to a mismatch; for an order that underbuilds, the first reference knot never made and why; the knot test of the reference structures.
comparators_or_controls: The reference engine's complete rounds; the gate with the demand compared and three altered controls; the earlier study's results under a fixed ration of three; the record's depth guard as control.
resource_budget: Each search under ten minutes and 8 GB where it can be, capped at two million states with no time budget; anything longer in a background unit with a memory cap and a row in the long-running index.
first_executable_signal: The gate; then every order of R3 on D2(4,3) under (CAP-3, CANCEL-WAIT, RELEASE) through round 1.
decision_rule: Each prediction is judged by its 'Fails when' column; checks and open items are reported as such.
stop_rule: In the owner's words: a match in every order searched, or the first mismatch; for holding, the first mismatch of R3 or of the repaired guard R3', or a match through the last cutoff. Every registered run done and every prediction with a verdict.
nonclaims: An exploratory study of supplied laws with a supplied record of parents, to the rounds searched. A match under the cap closes a named gap of the earlier study and shows nothing new about the model. A mismatch under holding shows that a brood is not one round's roster when a parent stays, and does not show that no guard works there. The cap with holding tests little on the registered starts.
